answer: Price identity the way a lagoon charges for water: every agent locks a refundable stake before trading, sized to the volume it moves. Spawning a thousand fakes costs a thousand deposits, while honest work earns the stake back with interest, so fakes starve and real agents profit. Reputation works like an opal — layered and hard to fake — because a rating counts only when the rater has staked and transacted. A cedar-style slow-growth rule caps how fast a new agent's influence rises, so a fresh swarm cannot flood the market unseen. Attackers pay capital and time; defenders only need patience.
